Both sexes in the colony (Table 1: male 85.4 +/- 0.65 kHz, n = 19, female 86 +/- 0.6 kHz, n = 18; the sex counts sum to 37 against the population n of 36). Table 1 caption: 'Biome category and mean (± SD) body mass and RF for each sampled population'; its footnote says an equal number of males and females were used to calculate the mean population mass and RF, yet the Table 1 sex counts are unequal and do not add to the population n; the Results say RF was measured for 248 individuals while the Table 1 population counts sum to 210. Eleven populations were sampled; Knysna (n = 4) and Sleepy Hollow (n = 2) are not filed because of their very small n. The Results report that RF differed significantly among populations (GLM, P < 0.001) and rose clinally from 75.7 kHz at Lekkersing in the west to 86.5 kHz at Baviaanskloof in the east; the Discussion calls the RF-habitat relationship solely correlative and notes the statistical non-independence of the populations. Recording was from hand-held bats, so the value is a resting frequency, not a free-flight call. No year of sampling is printed.
